exercise_bank.title: Count It Out
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the numbers out loud from 1 to 20, one at a time, at a steady pace.

exercise_bank.title: Days in Order
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the days of the week out loud in order, starting with Sunday.

exercise_bank.title: Months in Order
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the months of the year out loud in order, starting with January.

exercise_bank.title: Name What You See
exercise_bank.instructions: Here is a word: toothbrush. Say out loud one sentence describing what it is or what it's used for.

exercise_bank.title: Picture in Your Mind
exercise_bank.instructions: Picture a kitchen in your mind. Name out loud three objects you would expect to find there.

exercise_bank.title: Three Words, One Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Here are three words: dog, park, morning. Say one full sentence out loud that uses all three.

exercise_bank.title: Can't Find the Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Name an object you use to cut paper.

exercise_bank.title: Category Rapid Fire
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud as many animals as you can in one minute.

exercise_bank.title: Synonym Swap
exercise_bank.instructions: Here is a word: happy. Say a word out loud that means almost the same thing.

exercise_bank.title: Opposite Day
exercise_bank.instructions: Here is a word: hot. Say the opposite out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Verb Tense Shift
exercise_bank.instructions: Here is a verb: run. Say it out loud in the past tense, then in the future tense.

exercise_bank.title: Fix the Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Here is a sentence: She go to the store yesterday. Say the corrected version out loud.

exercise_bank.title: One-Step Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Sam folded a piece of paper in half. Say out loud: is the paper now bigger or smaller than before?

exercise_bank.title: Two-Step Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Ben picked up his phone, then put it in his pocket. Say out loud: where did Ben put his phone?

exercise_bank.title: Three-Step Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Priya stood up, walked to the door, then sat back down. Say out loud: what did Priya do right before sitting back down?

exercise_bank.title: Find the Match
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this description: it is round, orange, and you peel it before eating it. Say out loud what is being described.

exercise_bank.title: Yes or No Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: "The sun shines at night." Say out loud whether that is true or false.

exercise_bank.title: Where Is It
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Alex placed the keys under a book. Say out loud: which object ends up on top, the keys or the book?

exercise_bank.title: Between and Behind
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: a cup is placed behind a plate. Say out loud: which object is in front?

exercise_bank.title: Listen and Answer
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Maria packed her bag. She is going on a trip. Answer out loud: what was Maria doing?

exercise_bank.title: How Many Are Left
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Jamie has three apples and gives one to a friend. Say out loud: how many apples does Jamie have left?

exercise_bank.title: Bigger or Smaller
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: the red cup is bigger than the blue cup. Say out loud: which cup is smaller?

exercise_bank.title: Before or After
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: Noah finished his homework before dinner. Say out loud: did Noah do his homework before or after dinner?

exercise_bank.title: Open or Closed
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen: the store closes at 6pm. It is 6:30pm. Say out loud: is the store open or closed?

exercise_bank.title: Tongue Press Hold
exercise_bank.instructions: Press the tip of your tongue against the roof of your mouth just behind your teeth, hold for three seconds, then relax. Repeat five times, then say 'la la la' out loud three times to carry that same tongue placement into speech.

exercise_bank.title: Lip Round and Spread
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'oo-ee-oo-ee' out loud, rounding your lips fully on 'oo' and spreading them fully on 'ee'. Repeat ten times.

exercise_bank.title: Full Jaw Open and Close
exercise_bank.instructions: Open your jaw slowly as wide as is comfortable, then close it slowly. Repeat five times, then say 'ah' with a fully open jaw.

exercise_bank.title: Half-Speed Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud as slowly and clearly as you can, giving every word its own clear space: I would like a glass of water, please.

exercise_bank.title: Overarticulate Every Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud using big, exaggerated mouth movements on every sound, not just some: The big black cat sat on the mat.

exercise_bank.title: Louder Than Usual
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a full breath, then say this sentence out loud as loudly and clearly as you comfortably can, without straining your throat: My voice is strong and clear today.

exercise_bank.title: Tap to Pace
exercise_bank.instructions: Tap the table once for each word while you say this sentence out loud, keeping every tap evenly spaced: I am speaking one word at a time.

exercise_bank.title: One Breath, One Phrase
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a breath, then say this short phrase out loud in one breath: I feel good today. Pause, take another breath, and repeat it twice more.

exercise_bank.title: Pa-Ta-Ka
exercise_bank.instructions: Say "pa-ta-ka" out loud as quickly and clearly as you can, five times in a row.

exercise_bank.title: Cheek Puff Hold
exercise_bank.instructions: Puff out your cheeks with air and hold for three seconds without letting any air escape, then release. Repeat five times, then say "boom boom boom" out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Sharpen the S and Sh
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, giving extra clear emphasis to every 's' and 'sh' sound: She sells seashells by the seashore.

exercise_bank.title: Three Phrase Chunks
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud in three short phrases, pausing briefly between each: I need to go to the store / before it closes / so I should leave soon.

exercise_bank.title: Soft Start
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, starting the very first sound gently and gradually instead of with a hard push: Amazing things can happen today.

exercise_bank.title: Light Touch Consonants
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words out loud using a light, relaxed touch on the first sound instead of pressing hard: pat, bat, top, dot.

exercise_bank.title: Link It All Together
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this phrase out loud as one continuous flow of sound, without stopping airflow between words: I want to go outside and play.

exercise_bank.title: Stretch Every Syllable
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, stretching each syllable slightly longer than usual: We are walking to the store together.

exercise_bank.title: Chunk and Breathe
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud in three short chunks, taking a breath between each: I woke up early / and made breakfast / before school.

exercise_bank.title: Slow and Smooth Passage
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage out loud at a deliberately slower, smoother pace than normal: The morning sun rose over the quiet hills as birds began to sing.

exercise_bank.title: Pause and Restart Gently
exercise_bank.instructions: If a word ever feels stuck while you talk, pause fully for one second, then restart just that word slowly and gently before continuing.

exercise_bank.title: One Minute Easy Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk out loud for one minute about your morning, using a soft gentle start on the first word of every sentence.

exercise_bank.title: Ease Out of It
exercise_bank.instructions: If you feel a stutter happening while you're talking, ease out of it slowly and smoothly instead of pushing through, then keep going.

exercise_bank.title: Plan the Hard Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Think of a word that's often hard for you to start. Before saying it out loud, take a breath and plan a slow, easy first sound, then say the word.

exercise_bank.title: Even Steady Pace
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud at a slow, steady pace, giving each word equal, even timing: Slow and steady speech can feel more comfortable and controlled.

exercise_bank.title: Notice the Smooth Spots
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk out loud for thirty seconds about your favorite hobby. Afterward, say one moment that felt smooth and one that felt effortful.

exercise_bank.title: Gentle Hum Warm-Up
exercise_bank.instructions: Hum gently for five seconds, feeling a light buzzing or vibration around your lips and nose.

exercise_bank.title: Hum Into a Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Hum gently, then let the hum flow directly into the word 'hello' out loud, keeping that same forward, buzzy feeling.

exercise_bank.title: Sustain the Sound
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a comfortable breath, then hold a steady 'ee' sound out loud for as long as you comfortably can, without straining.

exercise_bank.title: Pitch Glide Up
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'ee' out loud, sliding your pitch smoothly from low to high like a gentle siren going up.

exercise_bank.title: Pitch Glide Down
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'oh' out loud, sliding your pitch smoothly from high to low like a gentle siren going down.

exercise_bank.title: Strong Short Bursts
exercise_bank.instructions: Say short, firm 'ee' sounds out loud at a few different comfortable pitches, keeping each one clear and easy, not strained.

exercise_bank.title: Vocal Habits Check-In
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud how much water you drank today and whether you did any shouting or a lot of throat-clearing.

exercise_bank.title: Carry the Buzz Into a Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Hum briefly, then say this full sentence out loud keeping that same easy, forward, buzzy voice feeling the whole time: My voice feels easy and comfortable.

exercise_bank.title: Yawn Sigh
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a big yawn, and as you breathe out, let out a relaxed "ahh" sound, letting your voice glide gently downward.

exercise_bank.title: Lip Trill
exercise_bank.instructions: Relax your lips and blow air gently through them to make a motorboat-like trill sound ("brrr"), then let the trill turn into a hum.

exercise_bank.title: Soft Start Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, starting every word with a soft, easy voice instead of a hard push: We can take it easy today.

exercise_bank.title: Natural Pitch Variation
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud, letting your pitch rise and fall naturally like you're telling an interesting story: I couldn't believe what happened next!
